newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia wants apology from Singapore's Lee over remarks.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia wants apology from Singapore's Lee over remarks.

text.p: The Malaysian government asked Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew on Wednesday to retract a statement criticising a Malaysian state.
"If the Senior Minister really values our goodwill, he should retract his statement and tender an apology," the Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said in a statement.
Abdullah said he was "extremely shocked at the sentiments and derogatory statement made by Mr Lee Kuan Yew, a Senior Minister of the Singapore government, on Johor".
In a court affidavit filed in a Singapore court on January 27, Lee described Malaysia's Johor state, just across a causeway from Singapore, as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".

Lee's affidavit was filed in one of 13 libel lawsuits brought against Singapore opposition politician Tang Liang Hong after elections in January. Tang left Singapore shortly after losing the election, saying that he feared for his life.
